what_our_tables_hold.news: 592,264 rows; title + a snippet of at most 400 characters (average 302). No article body is stored, so "long-form news" in our tables is short text today.
what_our_tables_hold.youtube_transcripts: 0 rows: the table exists and is empty. Captions for this test were fetched fresh with youtube-transcript-api (26 of 26 videos answered, about 0.9 s each, from this MacBook).
what_our_tables_hold.full_articles: fetched from the stored url with trafilatura for this test only: 58 of 100 gave more than 800 characters (median 4,233); the rest are paywalled, video pages or quote lists.

news_rubric: One label per news row, for the ticker the row is filed under, from the stored title + snippet only: B = plainly good for that name's price (approval, upgrade, buy call, beat, shares up), S = plainly bad (lawsuit, downgrade, closures, shares down, 'will never recover'), N = routine, comparison pieces with no winner stated, 13F fund-holding notices, quote-list pages, mixed, or the story is not about that name. A second flag marks rows where the story is not about the filed ticker at all. One labeller (the reviewing model), labelled before any model was run on news.
youtube_rubric: One label per video for the ticker the video is filed under: B = the speaker is plainly positive on that name (bought more, bullish deep-dive, 'undervalued', 'remain bullish'), S = plainly negative (sceptical teardown, 'downgraded', 'strong sell'), N = level maps, debates with both sides, day-trade recaps, news round-ups, 'not bearish but sold'. Labelled by one labeller (the reviewing model) from the title plus the passages that mention the name (not from watching the video), before any model ran.
caveat: One labeller. News: 100 labels (about plus or minus 9 points). Articles: 58, labelled from the title + snippet, not the full text. YouTube: 20 labels made from the passages naming the ticker (about plus or minus 20 points) — the passages-only arm reads the same passages the labeller read, which favours it.
